prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the mortgage-underwriting agent (residential mortgage applications and remortgages) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: identity documents for a new account. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 0)
response: {"items":[{"type":"observation","content":"When the applicant is opening a new account at the same time as the mortgage, I should check that the identity document names match the mortgage application exactly, including middle names where they are used consistently."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the passport or driving licence has expired, I should not treat it as acceptable evidence for new account opening, even if it is still being used informally elsewhere."},{"type":"observation","content":"When a document shows a different address from the application, I should treat that as normal only if the document is clearly still current enough for identity rather than address verification."},{"type":"preference","content":"When the customer provides a photo ID, I prefer to capture the document type, expiry date and issuing authority together so the new-account check is complete in one pass."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the name on the identity document includes a recent change, I should ask for a clear link to the current name before progressing the account opening."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the identity document is damaged, obscured or cut off in the upload, I should request a cleaner image rather than trying to infer missing details."},{"type":"observation","content":"When two different identity documents are provided, I should compare the core details carefully and not assume they match just because the photo looks similar."},{"type":"preference","content":"When evidence is borderline, I prefer to pause the new account setup and ask for an alternative document rather than risk carrying forward an uncertain identity match."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the customer is remortgaging and also opening a new account, I should remember that older mortgage records do not replace fresh identity verification for the new account."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the document is not in English or Welsh, I should treat it as needing extra verification before it can support new account opening."}]}
